subject.title: Telegram: specific forum topic becomes permanent inbound black hole after stuck-session recovery

question: Should Telegram timeout recovery release a stuck same-topic lane only after a hard cancellation/process-restart boundary, or should OpenClaw intentionally preserve the guarded-lane behavior and solve this with diagnostics/manual recovery instead?
rationale: The source-proven failure is real, but the safe recovery contract affects message ordering, session state, and whether old handler work may continue concurrently with later same-lane updates.

options.title: Require A Hard Boundary
options.body: Implement recovery so the timed-out update is failed and later same-lane updates drain only after the old handler is killed, isolated, or forced through a clean process restart boundary.

options.title: Preserve Guarding And Add Recovery UX
options.body: Keep serialization strict until the handler settles, but add operator-visible diagnostics and an in-product recovery path for stuck Telegram lanes.

options.title: Split Persistent-State Investigation
options.body: Treat the in-process guard as one tracker and separately investigate what state can survive full gateway restart for one forum topic.

recommendation.title: Require A Hard Boundary
recommendation.body: Implement recovery so the timed-out update is failed and later same-lane updates drain only after the old handler is killed, isolated, or forced through a clean process restart boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: Their review on the linked PR already framed the core safety choice between auto-release and a hard cancellation/process boundary.
